summary: Shipped af9c55145247b261: 1.0505x over amdclang (95% CI 1.0422-1.0585, 0.09938 ms vs 0.10442 ms, 77/77 battery cases). It is a source-level rewrite: the per-thread strided loop (8 iterations per thread at the bench shape) is gone; the launch is one 256-thread workgroup per 256 vec4 of a row (grid B*cdiv(D4,256), appended u32 arg cdiv(D4,256)), each thread loads one x vec4 and one y vec4, and stores one vec4. The math is x*rcp(1+exp2(-x*log2e))*y instead of expf plus IEEE division, so the result meets the manifest tolerance (rtol 1e-4) and is NOT bit-identical with amdclang. The kernel is memory-bound: cutting arithmetic from ~110 to ~40 instructions per vec4 alone measured parity, and all the gain (4-5%) comes from the loop-free short waves; every loop-free variant landed in 1.03-1.05 and they are not distinguishable from each other, so the margin is small and real but there is nothing further in reach.

friction: unroll_loads refuses masked loops (d89f65be97693948, .LBB0_2: 'the back edge is not s_cbranch_scc0 on a counter compare'). amdclang emits the exec-mask form (s_andn2_b64 exec + s_cbranch_execnz) for every per-thread strided loop, so the transform never applies to this family; I had to redo it at the source level (ecfd5adbc0f9f7d7).

No tool says what bounds a kernel. I inferred 'memory-bound' only by spending timed candidates (arithmetic cut 3x gave parity; loads in flight gave parity). A bytes-moved / achieved-bandwidth figure in bench or features (here about 400 MB in 0.1 ms) next to the device's known ceiling would have told me up front that only a few percent were available.

Paired bench results for near-identical states spread over 1.03 to 1.05 across runs with differing clock levels (1879 to 2400 MHz reported), so variants within about 2% of each other cannot be ranked; a way to bench two candidates against each other directly (not only against ref) would settle choices like block 64 vs 256 vs 1D vs 2D grid.
The reference clock state varies between benches (reference_ms 0.0987 to 0.1045 in this session), which makes it hard to compare candidate_ms across benches.
Whether a 2D grid is allowed in `launch` and whether __builtin_amdgcn_rcpf / __builtin_exp2f lower to v_rcp_f32 / v_exp_f32 are not documented in the skill files; both worked, found by trying.

exp2f lowers with denormal-range handling (cmp/cndmask/add/ldexp, 20 instructions per vec4) that is dead for 1+exp2(t); there is no source-level way to ask for the raw v_exp_f32, so it took a whole-body edit_ir (febc3c8bf7a909a9). A multi-delete by range in `edit` would have made that cheaper than retyping the body.
relaunch accepts a launch identical to the parent's and creates a new state (6a668085bb6855a4) instead of saying nothing changed.
